commands.review_summary:
The branch adds a capability-gated, parent-brokered pub/sub bus that delivers messages between sandboxed dashboard widgets on the same tab.

Reproducibility: yes. for the blocking PR defect: exact-head source inspection shows the directive can reuse a bridge whose callbacks closed over an earlier tab context. The proposed user-facing pub/sub behavior itself still lacks a real-browser reproduction.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Maintainers must first decide whether to sponsor the dashboard program and expanded widget boundary; contributor live proof, foundation landing, dependency authorization, and conflict resolution also remain human gates.

target.title: Dashboard: inter-widget pub/sub — a tab-scoped, parent-brokered message bus
target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map). > > 🧪 **Try this PR:** put two widgets on one tab that publish/subscribe → messages cross widgets **only within that tab**; other tabs stay isolated (verified server-side). --- > Widgets on the same tab can finally talk to each other — a filter widget drives a chart, a selector narrows a table — without ever being able to reach a widget on another tab. Closes #101147. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review `bus.ts` + the `bridge.ts` / host changes as the delta. ## What's in this PR - Bridge messages `dashboard:publish` / `dashboard:subscribe` / `dashboard:unsubscribe` (inbound) delivering as `dashboard:message` (outbound), gated behind a new `bus:pubsub` manifest capability. - A parent-brokered, DOM-free bus (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/bus.ts`): widgets never talk directly — the trusted parent fans a published payload out to the *other* same-tab subscribers on that channel. - Caps: 8 KB payload, 60 publishes / 60 s (keyed by stable widget name so a remount can't reset the budget), 256-char channel names. ## Security model (this is the point of the design) ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph TabA["Tab A — isolated bus"] PA["Widget A1 · publish"] --> BA{"Parent broker
tab-scoped · capability-gated
size + rate capped"} BA --> SA["Widget A2 · subscribe"] end subgraph TabB["Tab B — separate bus"] PB["Widget B1"] -.-> BB{"broker"} end BA -. "✗ never crosses tabs" .- BB ``` - **Tab isolation is structural, not a filter.** The subscription table is keyed `tabSlug → channel → subscriberId`, and a publish only ever iterates the *publisher's own tab bucket*. A widget on tab A cannot observe — or even enumerate — a subscriber on tab B; cross-tab delivery is unreachable code, not a rejected case. - **Identity is broker-assigned.** The host mints an opaque `subscriberId` the widget never sees, and binds `tabSlug` from the widget's real tab (`tab.slug` in `renderGrid`) — both are closed over in the parent; a child message only ever carries an opaque `channel` + `payload`. A widget can't spoof another's identity, target a specific peer, or name a tab it wasn't assigned to. The publisher is excluded from its own broadcast. - **No new reach.** The bus is in-memory and parent-brokered only — it never touches the gateway and never persists. The capability gate, size cap, and rate limit sit alongside the existing `sendPrompt` gates in `bridge.ts`; the `event.source` window-identity filter still guards the new inbound types; opaque origin unchanged. All of the above is covered by tests (same-tab delivery, cross-tab non-delivery, publisher exclusion, capability denial both directions, size/rate caps, unmount teardown, unexpected-window rejection). No new dependency. ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Dashboard widgets were fully isolated, so they couldn't compose — a filter widget had no way to drive a chart on the same tab. This adds a parent-brokered, tab-scoped pub/sub bus, capability-gated and rate/size-capped, with cross-tab isolation guaranteed by construction. **Evidence:** `pnpm -C ui vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/components` green including the bus/bridge/host suites (tab-isolation, publisher-exclusion, capability gate, caps, unmount sweep); `pnpm ui:i18n:check`, `pnpm ui:build`, and full type-aware oxlint clean. Counts confirmed by the submitting orchestrator's own gate run (not agent-reported).
